# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been on the shelf since the Clinton administration. Marisol Reyes found it while shelving returns: a faint pencil mark beside a passage about the moors, and in the margin, in small, careful handwriting, *"Heathcliff would not have said this. Too self-aware."*

She almost missed it. The pencil was so light it looked like a smudge until the light caught it. She checked the checkout card—yes, they still used cards in the Harborview Public Library, because Director Pham believed in them—and saw the book had been borrowed three times in the past month. Three different names.

The second note came two weeks later, in a biography of Charles Darwin. Beside a paragraph describing the Beagle's departure, the same hand had written: *"Wind was from the southwest that day. Author has it wrong."*
